These activities will advocate against proposed anti-biotechnology legislation and policies in Colombia and encourage wider understanding, acceptance, and adoption of biotechnology among key stakeholder groups. PURPOSE Since 2022, Colombia has remained open to the adoption of genetically engineered (GE)-derived commodities and other innovative technologies and has implemented various regulations facilitating GE cultivation and acceptance. Nevertheless, anti-biotechnology influences risk undoing decades of progress in this space and threaten U.S. market access of key GE commodities to the Colombian market. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have

PURPOSE Since 2022, Colombia has remained open to the adoption of genetically engineered (GE)-derived commodities and other innovative technologies and has implemented various regulations facilitating GE cultivation and acceptance. Nevertheless, anti-biotechnology influences risk undoing decades of progress in this space and threaten U.S. market access of key GE commodities to the Colombian market. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have successfully lobbied certain legislators to reject the science and the concept of biotechnology in general. Over six consecutive legislative years beginning in Page 3 of 6 July 2020, bills aimed at establishing “transgenic-free” municipalities, protecting farmers’ rights to save, reuse, and commercialize their seeds, and a GE seed ban have all been introduced in Congress. On November 2, 2023, Colombia’s Constitutional Court upheld a 2022 law mandating that the government take actions to protect indigenous land and native seeds and avoid risks derived from the release of living modified organisms from biotechnology processes. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have successfully lobbied certain legislators to reject the science and the concept of biotechnology in general. Over six consecutive legislative years beginning in Page 3 of 6 July 2020, bills aimed at establishing “transgenic-free” municipalities, protecting farmers’ rights to save, reuse, and commercialize their seeds, and a GE seed ban have all been introduced in Congress. On November 2, 2023, Colombia’s Constitutional Court upheld a 2022 law mandating that the government take actions to protect indigenous land and native seeds and avoid risks derived from the release of living modified organisms from biotechnology processes. In June 2026, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development published its legal review of the Court’s ruling and stated that Colombia will need to integrate new cultural impact assessments into the GE approval process. Personnel The Contractor shall be solely responsible fo r ensuring sufficient personnel are assigned to this requirement. Murphy VA Medical Center, 7400 Merton Minter Blvd, San Antonio, TX, 78229 through the El Paso VA Contracting Office, intends to solicit proposals from Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) contractors to provide Intraoperative Neuromonitoring (IONM) services under an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Contract (IDIQ), with an anticipated period of performance of a base year and four (4) one-year option periods. The VA anticipates issuing a solicitation for this requirement on or about 1 August 2026, with an estimated closing date for proposals on or about 30 August 2026. The solicitation will be available for download from https://sam.gov. Interested offerors will be responsible for downloading copies of solicitation (and any subsequent amendments) from that website, and no hard copies will be made available. The solicitation will provide full information to contractors about the proposal submission process. Prospective offerors are enc

on process. Prospective offerors are encouraged to register their interest in the solicitation on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website so that they are notified of the issuance of the solicitation and any amendments. The services required include: On-site Certified Neurophysiologic Intraoperative Monitoring (CNIM) technologists Remote oversight by Board-Certified Neurophysiologists (Neurology/Physiatry/DABNM/privileged Neurosurgeon) Full provision of all equipment, materials, disposable supplies, and IT connectivity Real-time IONM monitoring and communication with surgical teams 24/7/365 coverage with defined emergency response requirements Credentialing and privileging prior to clinical work Compliance with all VA Directives, infection control, immunizations, mandatory training, CME/CEU, QA logs, incident reporting, and documentation standards Services will be provided to VHA healthcare-eligible Veterans of the STVHCS. SCOPE The Contractor, and not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control actions necessary to meet the quality standards set forth by the contract. The QASP is not a part of the contract nor is it intended to duplicate the Contractor’s Management Plan. The purpose of this RFI is to gather industry input on how cloud-native COTS solutions, configurations, standard integrations and supporting services can best meet NATO’s needs. 2. Responses will assist in: x Identifying potential solutions that could deliver the target outcomes outlined in the Epic-Outcome Matrix (Annex B: Part 2) and their indicative costs; x Identifying solutions that are proven and deployed in public procurement settings; x Validating, challenging or refining the current planning assumptions and requirements; x Identifying security, hosting, data resi dency, supplier-access, records-management and accreditation considerations; and, x Identifying key risks, constr aints and alternative packaging, phasing or acquisition options that NCIA and relevant NATO stakeholders should consider in shaping any future solicitation. C. Background 1. NATO is pursuing digital transformation. Within this context, the digital enablement of sourcing and procurement processes has become a critical focus. Purpose The Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) seeks to procure a commercially available, cloud-based Adult Education instructional software platform (Software as a Service (SaaS)) to support the Adult Education component of the Family and Child Education (FACE) Program. The software shall meet the functional requirements identified in this Statement of Work and support the instructional, reporting, and data integration needs of the FACE Adult Education Program. The software shall provide evidence-based instructional resources that support adult learners with a variety of educational and workf

cation Instructional Software Platform (Software as a Service) • Standard software technical support • Documentation necessary to integrate the software with the FACE data management system The Bureau's Technical Assistance (TA) contractor will provide implementation support, programmatic training, coaching, and ongoing assistance to FACE sites. The Bureau's FACE Data Team will manage system integration, dashboard development, reporting, and data management. Accordingly, this contract is limited to the software platform, software licensing, software support, and technical documentation necessary to support integration. 4. Response: Currently, no. However, expected growth is 5 VA Medical Center campus per year for the foreseeable future. Each medical center is the size of a college campus and is estimated to take 5-10TB of storage each. Is ESRI software (ArcGIS Enterprise) the target for hosting and management of GIS data or is open-source technologies like GeoServer, QGIS, or other a potential for implementation? Response: QGIS and Mapbox both are approved for VA use but are not used within the EGT/GSSC/VA Indoor systems. ESRI and SQL Server software will be used for this implementation. ABOUT CAPACITY BUILDING Within CSD, Capacity Building (CB) serves as CISA’s enterprise cybersecurity services management arm for national stakeholders and the lead for Federal enterprise cybersecurity governance. CB enables its customers to manage cybersecurity risk by building their capacity to implement effective cybersecurity policies, tools, and procedures. CB helps stakeholders better manage cybersecurity risk by 1) Defining expectations for stakeholder cybersecurity; 2) Leading implementation and enforcement of cybersecurity requirements; 3) Managing CISA’s cybersecurity services portfolio; 4) Building capacity; and 5) Enhancing collective defense and readiness. 1.1.1. This contract intends to leverage the full buying power of the Federal Government for all cyber product needs. 1.1.1.1. The requested period of performance is September 24, 2026, through April 19, 2027, for a total of seven months. This period is intended to support completion of the remaining interface development activities through the planned Oracle Health production Go-Live for the Wisconsin market on January 16, 2027, followed by post-Go-Live stabilization and support.
